title: An element of order $q$ in $\mathbb{F}_{p^{q-1}}^{\times}$
statement: Let $p$ and $q$ be distinct prime numbers, and let $\mathbb{F}_{p^{q-1}}$ denote the finite field with $p^{q-1}$ elements. Then the multiplicative group $\mathbb{F}_{p^{q-1}}^{\times}$ contains a unit $u$ whose order is exactly $q$.
replaced:
If $p \neq q$ are primes, then the unit group of $\mathbb{F}_{p^{q-1}}$ contains an
element $u$ with $\mathrm{ord}(u) = q$.
